specification.inputs: DS:DX points to an unopened standard or extended FCB whose 8.3 filename/extension fields specify the current-directory search. AH=1Ah may set the DTA used for results. Pathnames are not supported. `?` is supported in all DOS versions; DOS 3.0 also supports `*`.
specification.outputs: AL=00h when a match is found and FFh on failure. On success the DTA contains an unopened FCB of the same type as the search FCB. For a standard FCB, DTA byte 0 is the resolved drive number and the next 32 bytes contain the directory entry. For an extended FCB, the DTA starts with its 7-byte prefix and then the drive number and directory data. FFh does not mean only that no matching file exists; malformed names and extended-FCB attribute mismatch are also documented causes.
specification.flags: AL is the documented status; CF is not specified as a status result.
specification.units: FCB drive codes are 0 for default, 1 for A:, and subsequent one-based values for subsequent drives. Name and extension use 8.3 fields; DTA search/result data is 33 bytes for a standard FCB or 40 bytes for an extended FCB.
specification.lifetime: The initial search specification in the FCB must remain unchanged if AH=12h continues the search. DTA is the search/result buffer. When drive code 0 is used, the resolved drive is retained for AH=12h calls using that FCB.

specification.inputs: DS:DX points to the same search FCB used in a successful AH=11h call. At least one `?` must occur in the filename or extension pattern, and the initial search specification must remain unchanged between continuation calls.
specification.outputs: AL=00h on success and FFh on failure. On success the current DTA contains the next unopened FCB of the same type as the search FCB. FFh is a search-function failure result and should not be inferred to identify only a nonexistent match.
specification.flags: AL is the documented status; CF is not specified as a status result.
specification.units: The search pattern uses 8.3 FCB fields. A successful standard-FCB result occupies 33 DTA bytes; an extended-FCB result occupies 40 DTA bytes.
specification.lifetime: Continues the current-directory search initialized by AH=11h, using the same unchanged FCB and DTA search context. A default drive resolved by AH=11h remains in use for subsequent AH=12h calls with that FCB, even if the default drive later changes.

specification.inputs: DS:DX points to a previously opened standard or extended FCB. The current DTA must hold one record of the FCB record size; the default record size is 128 bytes and can be changed in the FCB.
specification.outputs: AL=00h for a complete record, 01h for EOF with no data, 02h when a DTA segment-wrap error cancels the read, and 03h for EOF with a partial record. specification.units: FCB record size and DTA transfer length are bytes; position is represented by FCB block and record fields.
